requirements.name: No training on our data
requirements.standard: Vendor does not use our inputs or outputs to train or improve models.

evidence.quote: By default, Halyard may use Customer Content to improve and train its models.
evidence.reason: Training on inputs and outputs is permitted by default, and the customer must opt out to stop it, which contradicts the standard.

evidence.quote: Customer may opt out at any time in the workspace settings, and the opt-out applies to Customer Content submitted after it takes effect.
evidence.reason: The opt-out is not retroactive, so content submitted before opting out may remain used for training.

evidence.quote: Inputs and Outputs together are "Customer Content".
evidence.reason: This definition shows that the training permission covers both inputs and outputs.

evidence.quote: Halyard will treat Customer Content as Customer's Confidential Information.
evidence.reason: This confidentiality commitment is on a different topic and does not expressly bar training use.

requirements.name: Zero data retention available
requirements.standard: Vendor offers zero data retention for our inputs and outputs.

evidence.quote: Halyard retains Customer Content for 90 days on a rolling basis.
evidence.reason: The contract sets a standard 90-day retention of inputs and outputs and offers no zero-retention option.

evidence.quote: Following termination, Halyard deletes Customer Content within 90 days.
evidence.reason: Post-termination deletion can take up to 90 days, so data is not retained at zero.

evidence.quote: Inputs and Outputs together are "Customer Content".
evidence.reason: This definition shows that the retention clause covers both inputs and outputs, but it creates no commitment of its own.

evidence.quote: By default, Halyard may use Customer Content to improve and train its models.
evidence.reason: Default use of content for model training is inconsistent with zero data retention.

requirements.name: Retention limit
requirements.standard: Where ZDR is not used, our inputs and outputs are deleted no later than termination.

evidence.quote: Following termination, Halyard deletes Customer Content within 90 days.
evidence.reason: Deletion is allowed up to 90 days after termination, which is later than the standard's requirement of deletion no later than termination.

evidence.quote: Halyard retains Customer Content for 90 days on a rolling basis.
evidence.reason: This sets a rolling retention period during the term, which does not itself address deletion by termination but shows content is kept in the meantime.

evidence.quote: Inputs and Outputs together are "Customer Content".
evidence.reason: This definition shows that the retention and deletion terms cover both inputs and outputs.

requirements.name: Subprocessors
requirements.standard: Subprocessor list disclosed, advance notice of changes, and a right to object.

evidence.quote: Halyard's subprocessors are listed in its documentation.
evidence.reason: Halyard discloses its subprocessors in a list, which satisfies the disclosure element.

evidence.quote: Halyard will notify Customer of new subprocessors by updating that list
evidence.reason: Notice is given only by updating a list, with no commitment to advance notice before a new subprocessor starts, so the customer must monitor the list.

evidence.quote: Customer may object in writing within 15 days, in which case Halyard will work with Customer in good faith to address the objection.
evidence.reason: Customer has a right to object in writing, and Halyard commits to address objections in good faith.

needs_review: subprocessors: conflicting language (terms:sec-4, terms:sec-4 vs terms:sec-4); check order of precedence.

requirements.name: Output IP indemnity
requirements.standard: Vendor indemnifies us against third-party IP claims arising from AI output.

evidence.quote: Halyard will defend Customer against third-party claims that Outputs, as generated by the Service, infringe a third party's intellectual property rights.
evidence.reason: Halyard commits to defend Customer against third-party IP infringement claims over Outputs, which is the core of the standard.

evidence.quote: "Outputs" means content the Service generates.
evidence.reason: Defines Outputs, which sets the scope of the indemnity in Section 8.

evidence.quote: Customer owns its Outputs.
evidence.reason: Addresses ownership of Outputs, a different topic from IP indemnity.

requirements.name: Confidentiality
requirements.standard: Our inputs and outputs are treated as our Confidential Information.

evidence.quote: Halyard will treat Customer Content as Customer's Confidential Information.
evidence.reason: Customer Content, defined as Inputs and Outputs together, is committed to be treated as Customer's Confidential Information, which is exactly what the standard asks.

evidence.quote: Inputs and Outputs together are "Customer Content".
evidence.reason: This definition makes the confidentiality clause cover both inputs and outputs.

evidence.quote: By default, Halyard may use Customer Content to improve and train its models.
evidence.reason: Default permission to use Customer Content for model training sits uneasily with treating it as Customer's Confidential Information, and the customer must opt out, which also applies only to content submitted afterward.

needs_review: confidentiality: conflicting language (terms:sec-6 vs terms:sec-2); check order of precedence.

requirements.name: Security commitments
requirements.standard: SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001, plus notice of a security breach affecting our data within 72 hours.

evidence.quote: Halyard maintains a SOC 2 Type II report and will notify Customer of a security breach affecting Customer Content within 72 hours.
evidence.reason: Halyard commits to maintaining a SOC 2 Type II report and to notifying Customer of a security breach affecting Customer Content within 72 hours, matching both parts of the standard.

requirements.name: Output ownership
requirements.standard: We own the AI outputs, or the vendor assigns its rights in them to us.

evidence.quote: Customer owns its Outputs.
evidence.reason: The vendor states plainly that the customer owns the AI outputs, which is what the standard asks for.

evidence.quote: "Outputs" means content the Service generates.
evidence.reason: This defines Outputs, so the ownership clause covers all content the Service generates, but it does not itself grant ownership.
